prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t name one single “best” roofing company for all Dallas roof replacements — the right contractor depends on your roof size/material, budget, warranty needs, insurance situation, and your location. Instead, here’s a quick plan to find the best company for your job and what to check when you talk to them. If you want, I can pull top-rated local companies for your ZIP code and compare 3 estimates for you.

How to find the best roofer for your replacement
- Get multiple written estimates (3 is a good target). Compare scope, materials, timeline, and total cost — not just the bottom line.
- Prefer contractors with manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed Select ShingleMaster, etc.) — these let you access stronger manufacturer warranties.
- Check local reviews (Google, Yelp), BBB rating, and recent photos of finished jobs in Dallas neighborhoods similar to yours.
- Ask for references and call at least two recent customers to verify quality and timeliness.
- Make sure they are locally based (not storm-chasers), have a physical address, and can get local permits.
- Verify insurance: ask for supplier and roofer insurance certificates (general liability and workers’ comp) and confirm they’re current.
- Get lien waivers and a written warranty that clearly states workmanship coverage and how long it lasts.
- Request a detailed contract listing materials (brand/model/color), tear-off or overlay, number of shingles per square, flashing details, ventilation, disposal of old materials, start/end dates, and payment schedule.

Important questions to ask each company
- Are you licensed and insured in Texas? Can I see proof?
- Are you local to Dallas and how long have you worked here?
- Are you a certified installer for the shingle brand I want?
- Do you handle permits and inspections?
- What does your workmanship warranty cover and for how long?
- How will you protect my landscaping, gutters, and driveway during the job?
- Who will supervise the crew and how will I contact them?
- Do you provide a written estimate with line-item details?

Red flags to avoid
- High-pressure “sign today” offers or insisting you must replace immediately without documentation (storm chasers).
- No physical address or only a PO box.
- Asking for full payment up front — a reasonable deposit is typical, but not 100%.
- No proof of insurance or unwillingness to provide references.
- Extremely low bids that look too good to be true.

If you want, I can:
- Look up 3–5 top-rated roofing companies in Dallas (I’ll include ratings, certifications, and red flags) — tell me your ZIP code.
- Review estimates (you can paste them here) and point out differences and likely best value.

Which would you like me to do next?
